name: Cagliari Elmas Airport
before:
Sardinia's southern gateway, 7 km from Cagliari and unusually easy to leave. The airport has its own railway station, and from it the Sardinian rail network reaches most towns on the island, so a client without a hire car is not stranded at the door.

The terminal was expanded in 2003 and fitted with six jetbridges, taking it to a capacity of four million passengers a year. It passed that in 2018, handling just over 4.37 million, so expect it to be busy at peak times in summer.

It opened in May 1937 and has been the island's main airport in the south ever since. The airport stands in the territory of Elmas rather than Cagliari itself, which is why it appears on some schedules as Cagliari Elmas.
after:
Sardinia's gateway at Cagliari, 7 km from the city centre and unusually easy to leave. The airport has its own railway station, and from it trains reach the island's main towns, so a client without a hire car is not stranded at the door.

Its terminal was expanded in 2003. It handled about 5.3 million passengers in 2025, so expect it to be busy at peak times in summer.

The airport stands in the territory of Elmas rather than Cagliari itself, which is why it appears on some schedules as Cagliari Elmas.

claims.note: Was 'Sardinia's southern gateway'. Cagliari is the southernmost of the three Sardinian airports with scheduled service (OurAirports: 39.25 N against 40.63 and 40.90), but no saved source uses the word south, so the compass word is dropped (see the cut).

claims.why: True by the coordinates, but no saved source (operator, Wikipedia, Eurostat, Assaeroporti) calls the airport southern, so the gate's bearing check cannot pass it. Reworded to 'Sardinia's gateway at Cagliari'.

claims.wasBefore: taking it to a capacity of four million passengers a year. It passed that in 2018, handling just over 4.37 million
claims.why: The capacity rests on Wikipedia alone (the operator's pages do not give one, and its masterplan page has no text). The 2018 figure is right but stale, and is replaced by 2025's (see above).
Wikipedia alone. The operator's history starts with the company in 1990; the Italian Air Force site did not answer tonight (see Bari).

claims.why: 'Ever since' 1937 rests on Wikipedia alone. Its place as Sardinia's southern airport stays in the first sentence, from OurAirports and the 2025 tables.
